metadata.design_intent: 56x92m three-lane Levantine old-city bazaar with irregular spatial beats, courtyards, covered souk passages, and one shared 1.4m terrace loop.

districts.label: Spice Street
districts.notes: Warm limestone shopfronts, spice sacks, teal shutters, and cloth shade.

districts.label: Fountain Court
districts.notes: Hero courtyard with blue tile accents and an off-center fountain.

districts.label: Textile Arcade
districts.notes: Compressed shaded arcade with hanging rugs and patterned cloth.

districts.label: Rug Gate
districts.notes: Rug merchants and the framed northern gate approach.

districts.label: Caravan Court and Tea Terrace
districts.notes: Service storage below and a lived-in raised tea terrace.

districts.label: Dyers Souk
districts.notes: Ochre plaster, dye vessels, covered passages, and a quiet dogleg.

layoutIntent.composition: Named trade recesses and closed household/service entries retain their axes, with one complete upper closure on each axis and clear door approaches.
One household entry on the axis with the retained screened window aligned above it; the shared merchant block owns the backing and roof.
Two sealed inspection panels articulate the solid retaining enclosure; upper bindings remain dormant.
Two high blind niches sit at thirds; the redundant upper niche remains a dormant binding.
Yard wall on the spine: two niches at the third points with two above them, string course, nothing else (the grammar wants two bays on a 9.3 m span).

1.9 m blank return of the same house in cut stone (the validator wants adjacent frontages to differ in material): one pilaster on its axis.
Niche, door, niche, door, niche march at one 1.545 m gap under one 2.5 m head: the two storage doors mirror about the court axis, a niche holds the axis and one closes each held corner.

Yard wall: two niches at the third points (a 6 m span needs two bays).
A door on the axis of the house with one dark-recess window mirrored each side, 1.25 m piers holding the corners; the limewash marks it as the older of the two houses.
Two blind niches at equal 1.82 m gaps flank the axis of the yard where the dyers rack hangs; the wall is a working wall, its door is the cart gate in the Dogleg.
One high blind niche matches the opposite link wall; the lower field and turning space stay clear.
A garden wall closing the connector: coping, one string course, and a single blind niche on the axis of the approach from Tea Landing; the stone quoins hold both corners.
Spawn edge wall, 2.6 m, cut stone: one niche on the axis, corners open by size.
Spawn edge wall: one niche on the axis.

Yard wall: string course and one blind niche on the axis, held corners. Replaces the timber closure that pretended to be a door.
